result.topic_en: Gauss integrates the differential equations of precession in right ascension and declination, shows how to determine the four constants from two epochs, and applies this to the Pole Star, tabulating its positions for several years.
result.transcription:
15.
Praecession

Es sei $\alpha$ Rectascension, $\delta$ Declination und
$\frac{d\alpha}{dt} = m + n\tan\delta\sin\alpha$
$\frac{d\delta}{dt} = n\cos\alpha$

Das Integral dieser Gleichungen wird, wenn man Kürze halber $m=\theta\cos\varepsilon$, $n=\theta\sin\varepsilon$ setzt
$\sin\delta = \cos A\sin\varepsilon\sin(B+\theta t) + \sin A\cos\varepsilon$
$\cos\delta\sin\alpha = \cos A\cos\varepsilon\sin(B+\theta t) - \sin A\sin\varepsilon$
$\cos\delta\cos\alpha = \cos A\cos(B+\theta t)$

Die Werthe der vier Constanten $A, B, \varepsilon, \theta$ sind aus zwei Oertern bestimmbar. Man hat nämlich

$\cos\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta).\sin\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta) = \cos A\cos(B+\tfrac12\theta(t+t'))\sin\tfrac12\theta.(t'-t).\sin\varepsilon$
$\left.\begin{array}{l}\cos\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta).\cos\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta).\cos\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha)\sin\tfrac12(\alpha'-\alpha)\\ -\sin\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta).\sin\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta).\sin\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha).\cos\tfrac12(\alpha'-\alpha)\end{array}\right\} = \cos A\cos(B+\tfrac12\theta(t+t')).\sin\tfrac12\theta(t'-t).\cos\varepsilon$

$\left.\begin{array}{l}\cos\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta)\cos\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta).\sin\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha).\sin\tfrac12(\alpha'-\alpha)\\ +\sin\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta)\sin\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta).\cos\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha).\cos\tfrac12(\alpha'-\alpha)\end{array}\right\} = \cos A\sin(B+\tfrac12\theta(t+t')).\sin\tfrac12\theta(t'-t)$
$\left.\begin{array}{l}\cos\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta).\cos\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta).\cos\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha).\cos\tfrac12(\alpha'-\alpha)\\ +\sin\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta).\sin\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta).\sin\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha).\sin\tfrac12(\alpha'-\alpha)\end{array}\right\} = \cos A\cos(B+\tfrac12\theta(t+t')).\cos\tfrac12\theta(t'-t)$

Man setze demnach $\cot\tfrac12(\delta'-\delta)\cos\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha) = M\cos\psi$, $\tan\tfrac12(\delta'+\delta).\sin\tfrac12(\alpha'+\alpha) = M\sin\psi$ so wird
$\cot\varepsilon = M\sin[\tfrac12(\alpha'-\alpha)-\psi]$ ; $\tan\tfrac12(t'-t)\theta = \frac{\tan(\frac12(\alpha'-\alpha)-\psi)}{\cos\varepsilon}$
und demnächst $\frac{\tan\delta}{\sin\alpha} = \tan\omega$, $\frac{\cos(\omega-\varepsilon)}{\cos\omega}\tan\alpha = \tan(B+\theta t)$, $\tan(\omega-\varepsilon)\sin(B+\theta t) = \tan A$

Für den Polarstern setzen wir für 1750 $\delta = 87^\circ 58' 2''40$ $\alpha = 10^\circ 41' 0''10$
1812 $\delta' = 88\ 18\ 18,81$ $\alpha' = 13\ 46\ 22''50$

Hieraus $\varepsilon = 22^\circ 22' 56''66$, $62\theta = 27' 14''012$, $\theta = 52''71$, $m = 48''738$, $n = 20''071$, $A = 67^\circ 9' 28''00$ O 31 B.dl[?]
B für 1781 .... $85^\circ 18' 9''33$. Setzt man $87^\circ 39' 4''67 + 26''355(t-1781) = \Delta$ so und
$7.6034309\sin\Delta = \sin\zeta\sin P$
$9.5848893\cos\Delta = \sin\zeta\cos P$
$9.9652617\cos\Delta = \cos\zeta\sin Q$
so wird von selbst $9.9999965\sin\Delta = \cos\zeta\cos Q$
und $\delta = 90^\circ - 2\zeta$[?]
$\alpha = P - Q$
So findet sich $\alpha$ $\delta$
1690 $8^\circ 25' 27''67$ $87^\circ 38' 14''74$
1790 12. 33. 47,08 88 11 8,84
1800 13. 5. 42,84 88 14 24,54
1801[?] 13 9 57,91 88 14 48,80
1804 13. 18. 58,42 88 15 42,69
1754 10 51 20,75 87 59 21,44

methods.what: Differential equations of precession in right ascension and declination
Closed-form integral of the precession equations (rotation about a fixed axis)
Half-angle relations between two positions for determining the constants
Auxiliary angle psi to compute epsilon and theta from two positions
Determination of B and A via auxiliary angle omega
Numerical constants for the Pole Star
Logarithmic computation scheme for Pole Star positions with auxiliary angles P, Q, zeta

items.quote: Die Werthe der vier Constanten $A, B, \varepsilon, \theta$ sind aus zwei Oertern bestimmbar.
items.english: The values of the four constants A, B, epsilon, theta can be determined from two positions.
